sentences.text:
X (Juvenile In Conflict With Law) ... vs State Of Uttarakhand on 3
January, 2026
Author: Ravindra Maithani
Bench: Ravindra Maithani
 High Court Of Uttarakhand At Nainital
 Bail Application (Ia) No.01 of 2025
 In
 Criminal Appeal No. 574 of 2025
X (Juvenile in conflict with law) ........Appellant/Applicant
 Vs.
State of Uttarakhand ........... Respondent
Present : Mr. R.P. Nautiyal, Senior Advocate assisted by Mr. Vinay Bisht,
 Advocate for the appellant/applicant.

entities.text: High Court Of Uttarakhand At Nainital
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Ms. Manisha Rana Singh, Deputy Advocate General for the State.
Hon'ble Ravindra Maithani, J. (Oral)

Instant appeal is preferred against the judgment and order dated 15.09.2025, passed in Special Sessions Trial No. 38 of 2024, State of Uttarakhand Vs. X, by the court of Special Judge (POCSO)/Additional Sessions Judged, Dehradun.
By it, the appellant has been convicted under Sections 363, 376 IPC and Section 3/4 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 and he has been sentenced accordingly.

entities.text: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The appellant seeks bail during pendency of the appeal.
2. The appeal is already admitted.

3. Heard on Bail Application (IA) No.01 of 2025.
4.
Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.

5. Learned Senior Counsel appearing for the appellant submits that the appellant was on bail during trial; he never misused the bail; there is no impediment in grant of bail to the appellant and suspension of sentence as the proviso to Section 12 of The Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015 ("the Act") does not come into play.

entities.text: Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 6. Learned State Counsel would submit that the applicant is a convict; his appeal is to be heard as appeals are heard under the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 ("the Code") in view of Section 103 of the Act; the prosecution has proved his case beyond reasonable doubt.

entities.text: X (Juvenile In Conflict With Law) ... vs State Of Uttarakhand
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This Court has today, in CRLA No.326 of 2024, T vs. State of Uttarakhand, already held that while considering bail of a CIL post conviction, the provisions of Section 12 of the Act will still come into play.

8. The appellant was on bail during trial, nothing has been brought that if released on bail, the appellant would come into association with any known criminal or exposes him to any moral,
physical or psychological danger or his release, in any manner, may defeat the ends of justice.
9. Having considered, this Court is of the view that it is a case in which the execution of sentence should be suspended and the applicant/appellant be enlarged on bail.
10. The bail application is allowed.
11. The execution of sentence, which is under challenge in this appeal shall remain suspended during the pendency of the appeal.

12. Let the applicant/appellant be released on bail, during pendency of the appeal on his executing a personal bond and furnishing two reliable sureties, each of the like amount, to the satisfaction of the court concerned.
13.
List in due course.

(Ravindra Maithani, J.) 03.01.2026 Sanjay X (Juvenile In Conflict With Law) ... vs State Of Uttarakhand on 3 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/123330715/
